correctness.rationale: For fixed interior fitness, subcritical birth–death with total clearing is regenerative and has a unique stationary law. The stationary reset age is Exp(R); Poisson immigration conditioned on that age yields an exact exponential cluster PGF. First-order immigration expansion at input a/v and iid site multiplication give a proper CP law with intensities a∫exp(−Rt)P(Z_t=n)dt. The exact one-founder geometric formula follows from its Riccati generating-function equation. In the edge scaling w=1−l, nR→s with R∼Cw^nu, 0<nu<1, nw→0; for t=ny, n²P(Z_t=n)→y⁻²exp(−1/y). A split-integral majorant on y<1/n, 1/n≤y≤1, y≥1 proves limit exchange; a(l)→1 follows from finite rho and q(1)=0. Bessel representation gives the stated profile and endpoints. The embedded standard-library checker passes 319 exact/numerical assertions; finite tests are corroborative, not proof.

value.rationale: Fixed-order moments of rare fitness levels can diverge and are already understood; they cannot determine the detailed moving-index law of the actual clustered jump sizes. The exact universal nR-scale Lévy profile and stretched-exponential Bessel cutoff give a directly interpretable description of rare large immigrant families, distinct from a routine higher-moment increment. The result supplies a testable family-size scaling function and separates critical log-series behavior from resetting-induced cutoff. Its exact domain, limit order and parameter range prevent claims of a general network phase transition.
